understanding: OKO is a home-security pipeline (camera → YOLO detector → tracker → zone resolver → event builder → deterministic decision engine → strict Bridge JSON) with an on-demand VLM gate that calls Google Gemini only for qualifying high-risk events. The 'OKO VLM' track was built chapter-by-chapter: Ch1 real GeminiVlmProvider, Ch2+3 assembly, Ch4.1 multi-frame request, Ch4.2 gate fail-safe prompt, Ch4.3 JPEG frame codec, Ch4.4 live wiring with debounce/cooldown. The code is ALREADY atomic and well-tested (src/oko/{domain,providers,vlm,tracking,zones,events,decision,bridge,pipeline,live,config}; ~189+ tests across phases). So Chapter 5 (final) is NOT a feature chapter — it is a final assembly + acceptance chapter: compose the existing atoms into one HONEST end-to-end VLM demo (real Gemini call, verbatim response, reproducible), keep the code modular ('по атомам' = the PROGRESS.md atom-table convention used in prior phases), and prepare a formal acceptance package. The repeated 'честное демо' instruction is a hard constraint reacting to a project history of auto-driver commits where a fabricated/mocked demo would be the main failure mode.
summary: Deliver Chapter 5 as a thin final assembly, not new architecture: compose the existing atoms (frame_codec → VlmGate → GeminiVlmProvider → LivePipeline) into one honest, reproducible real-Gemini end-to-end demo using the key already present at ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json, capturing the VERBATIM Gemini response + latency + frame ids + exact command as committed evidence. Back it with a deterministic OFFLINE acceptance test (injected transport, asserts wiring/payload shape — never real model text) so CI stays green, surface real-call failures honestly instead of relying on the gate's production fail-open swallow, update the PROGRESS.md Chapter-5 atom table + README acceptance section, run lint/type/format over the new atoms, then present the acceptance checklist and request operator sign-off. Changes stay thin, additive, and standards-clean because this is the final iteration.

decision_atoms.statement: The 'honest demo' MUST be a real network call to Gemini using the existing key (env GEMINI_API_KEY, else ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json geminiApiKey), committing the verbatim model response text, latency_ms, model id, prompt, and source frame ids; no mocked/hand-written output may be presented as the demo result.
decision_atoms.reason: success_tests require an honest demo and the constraint 'reflect the true state of the code'; project history of auto-driver commits makes a fabricated demo the single highest-impact failure. Reviewers must be able to re-run and reproduce.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Introduces nondeterminism, API cost, and a network/key dependency into the demo; if the key is rate-limited or egress is blocked the demo cannot 'succeed' and must fail visibly rather than be faked.

decision_atoms.statement: Separate two verification tiers explicitly: (a) an OFFLINE deterministic acceptance test using an injected transport that asserts the frames→gate→Gemini-payload→Bridge wiring and never asserts on real model prose; (b) an ONLINE one-shot honest demo that is evidence-only, not a pass/fail unit test.
decision_atoms.reason: The automated suite must stay green and deterministic without network access, while honesty requires a real run; conflating them produces either a flaky test or a fake demo.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Two artifacts to build and maintain (a test plus an evidence run), and reviewers must understand the offline test does not by itself prove the real API works.

decision_atoms.statement: Assemble Chapter 5 by composing existing atomic modules; add only thin atoms — a demo entrypoint, an evidence-writer, an end-to-end acceptance test, and a docs/atom-table update — rather than a new monolithic demo script or a parallel pipeline.
decision_atoms.reason: The codebase is already modular and the VLM path (frame_codec, VlmGate, GeminiVlmProvider, LivePipeline debounce) is complete and tested; the value-add of a final chapter is composition + evidence + sign-off, and DRY keeps one source of truth for wiring.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Less visible 'new code' to show for a chapter, and it requires touching/extending shared live entrypoints (oko.live.webcam / oko.pipeline.live) to surface the VLM response, risking regressions in existing live tests.

decision_atoms.statement: The demo path must surface VLM provider errors explicitly (exit nonzero, clear message) and never emit a fabricated description; do NOT rely on VlmGate.query_if_needed's production 'except Exception: response = None' fail-open, which would silently render a failed real call as 'no VLM response'.
decision_atoms.reason: Reading gate.py and test_pipeline_vlm_provider_error_does_not_fail_event confirms the production path intentionally swallows provider errors so events still flow — correct for production, but in a demo it hides a failed real Gemini call and reads as honest 'no result' when it is actually an error.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires a demo-specific error path distinct from production fail-open behavior, i.e. the demo checks the outcome/raw error rather than just the swallowed None.

decision_atoms.statement: Run a readiness preflight (reuse LiveReadinessChecker) before the demo; if the key/endpoint/network is unavailable, report 'blocked' honestly and abort — do not substitute fake camera/fake VLM output and call it the demo.
decision_atoms.reason: Prior phases already gate real runs behind readiness; honesty means a blocked demo is reported as blocked, matching the project's established 'real smoke blocked on credentials' pattern instead of silently downgrading to fakes.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: The demo may not run on demand in a constrained environment, forcing an explicit blocked status rather than a green checkmark.

decision_atoms.statement: Define formal acceptance as a concrete checklist: full pytest suite green (incl. the new offline VLM acceptance test), committed verbatim real-run evidence with a reproducible command, PROGRESS.md Chapter-5 atom table + README acceptance entry, lint/type/format clean, and committed-log secret scrubbing — then REQUEST operator sign-off (I prepare and request acceptance; I cannot self-grant it).
decision_atoms.reason: output_format asks for a readiness/acceptance report; success_tests demand demonstrable modular refactor, honest demo, passing tests, standards adherence, and stakeholder acceptance — which is an external human gate.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Final acceptance depends on an external stakeholder, so the deliverable is 'acceptance package + request', not a unilaterally claimed acceptance.

decision_atoms.statement: Hold scope to assembly + demo + acceptance + light modular cleanup; defer new VLM features (streaming, structured/JSON response parsing, multi-camera fan-out, on-image annotations) to a follow-up, not Chapter 5.
decision_atoms.reason: This is explicitly the final iteration and the instruction is 'СБОРКА не обсуждение' (assembly, not discussion); adding features now reintroduces risk and undermines the 'final, honest, accepted' goal.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Known nice-to-haves stay unbuilt and must be tracked as future work rather than landed here.

assumptions: 'По атомам' means the PROGRESS.md atom-decomposition convention used in prior phases (atom → file(s) → test → status table), not a brand-new architecture.
A valid Gemini API key is available at ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json (geminiApiKey) — verified present — and outbound HTTPS to generativelanguage.googleapis.com is permitted for the demo.
'Formal acceptance' requires a human operator/stakeholder sign-off; the agent can produce and submit the acceptance package but cannot grant acceptance itself.

runs/vlm-demo-frame.png is from an earlier demo attempt; Chapter 5 should produce/refresh comparable evidence that additionally includes the verbatim Gemini text response and latency, not just a frame.
The existing test suite (~189+ tests) is currently green; pytest could not be executed in this session (requires approval), so confirming green is part of the acceptance work, not a given.
Runtime is CPython 3.14 (per __pycache__ tags) while pyproject targets 3.11+; the demo and tests must run on the actual installed interpreter.
The committed live-webcam config and weights (models/yolov8n.pt / yolo11m.pt) remain valid for capturing real frames to feed the demo.

risks.risk: Dishonest or over-claimed demo: mocked/hand-written VLM text presented as a real Gemini response, or an 'expected' transcript passed off as live output.
risks.mitigation: Commit the verbatim raw Gemini response, latency, model id, prompt, and frame ids plus the exact reproducible command; keep the real call distinct from injected-transport tests; have the reviewer re-run before sign-off.

risks.risk: Secret or PII leakage in committed evidence: API key in headers/logs, or identifiable persons in committed demo frames sent to Google.
risks.mitigation: Scrub x-goog-api-key and any secrets from committed logs; never commit the key; use a benign staged scene for the demo and document the third-party data-egress in the runbook.

risks.risk: Real API dependency at demo time: key invalid, rate-limited, or network blocked, so the demo cannot run on demand.
risks.mitigation: Run LiveReadinessChecker preflight; on any blocker report an explicit 'blocked' status and abort nonzero — never downgrade to fakes; record the blocker in the acceptance report.

risks.risk: Gate's production fail-open swallow hides a failed real call, making a demo error look like a legitimate 'no VLM result'.
risks.mitigation: Demo path inspects the raw provider call/error explicitly and exits nonzero on failure, leaving the production fail-open behavior (and its test) untouched.

risks.risk: Refactor/assembly regressions: extending shared live entrypoints to surface the VLM response breaks existing live/pipeline tests.
risks.mitigation: Keep changes thin and additive; run the full pytest suite before and after; gate acceptance on a green run and add the new test alongside, not in place of, existing ones.

risks.risk: Flaky acceptance test if it asserts on real, nondeterministic Gemini prose.
risks.mitigation: Offline acceptance asserts only on request/payload shape and wiring via injected transport; the online demo is evidence-only and excluded from the deterministic suite.

risks.risk: Scope creep on the final chapter: features added instead of assembling, delaying or undermining acceptance.
risks.mitigation: Enforce a fixed Chapter-5 atom list and an 'assembly-only, final iteration' rule; record any feature ideas as deferred follow-ups in PROGRESS.md.

minimal_version: Compose the existing atomic modules into one honest end-to-end VLM demo: capture a few real webcam/staged frames, JPEG-base64 encode them via oko.vlm.frame_codec, run them through the existing VlmGate + GeminiVlmProvider using the real key from ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json, and print the Bridge JSON alongside the VERBATIM Gemini description; write run id, model, prompt, frame ids, response text, latency, and exit code to runs/ as committed, secret-scrubbed evidence with the exact reproducible command. Add ONE offline deterministic end-to-end VLM acceptance test (injected transport) asserting the frames→gate→Gemini-payload→Bridge wiring (never real prose). Surface provider/key errors honestly (nonzero, no fabricated text). Confirm the full pytest suite is green, update the PROGRESS.md Chapter-5 atom table and README acceptance section, run lint/format/type, then present the acceptance checklist and request operator sign-off.
advanced_version: All of minimal, plus: a dedicated thin `oko.vlm.demo` entrypoint atom that enables the gate, emits a structured evidence manifest (run id, model, frame ids, prompt, verbatim response, latency, exit code) and prints it next to the Bridge JSON; a LiveReadinessChecker preflight that makes the demo refuse (nonzero, 'blocked') rather than fall back to fakes when the key/network is absent; a record-once/replay-via-injected-transport regression harness so the real Gemini response becomes a labeled fixture (honestly noting it was captured live, not synthesized) giving deterministic coverage of the real payload shape; secret-scrubbing of all committed logs; a short DEMO.md runbook documenting the exact command, the third-party data egress, and the honest failure modes; and a ruff/black/mypy standards pass scoped to the Chapter-5 atoms with the atom→file→test→status table fully filled in PROGRESS.md and a Chapter-5 acceptance entry mirroring the prior-phase format for operator sign-off.
